chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Ḍurays al-Kunāsī, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

"If the male slave confesses against himself once before the Imam that he stole, he is to have his hand cut off; and if the female slave confesses against herself before the Imam to theft, her hand is to be cut off."

Because the proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it to mean that if proof is added to the confession, then the ruling applies; but as for mere confession alone, there is no amputation upon the two of them, in accordance with what the first report contained.

key_terms.أَقَرَّ: he confessed or admitted against himself
key_terms.الْأَمَةُ: the female slave under legal discussion
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam as the judicial authority before whom the confession is made
key_terms.الْعَبْدُ: the male slave under legal discussion
key_terms.قَطَعَهُ: he cut him, meaning the legal amputation penalty was carried out upon him

ai.seo_question: Does a single confession before the Imam establish the hadd punishment for theft for a slave?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling of theft in the case of a slave man or slave woman who confesses before the Imam. The accompanying explanation clarifies that the report is to be understood as applying when corroborating evidence accompanies the confession, whereas confession alone does not establish the punishment according to the earlier report.
